l: salvation in the kingdom of God, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Salvation in the kingdom of God requires charity, faith, and hope. Those without charity, faith, or hope cannot be saved in the kingdom of God.

l: kingdom of God, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: The kingdom of God is the place in which people cannot be saved without charity, faith, and hope. Those who do evil and die in their sins cannot be saved in the kingdom of God.

l: unbelief, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Unbelief can cause the spiritual gifts and power of God to be done away among people. Spiritual gifts continue only according to the unbelief of the children of men.

l: power of God, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: The power of God is not to be denied, because God works by power according to the faith of the children of men. If a person does good, that person works by the power and gifts of God, and denying that power prevents perfection in Christ.

l: Spirit of God, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: The Spirit of God manifests spiritual gifts unto men to profit them. Through it, different people receive wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, visions of angels and ministering spirits, tongues, and interpretation.

l: truth, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Truth is manifested by God through the power of the Holy Ghost to those who ask with a sincere heart, real intent, and faith in Christ. By the power of the Holy Ghost, people may know the truth of all things.

l: covenants of the Eternal Father, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: The covenants of the Eternal Father made with the house of Israel are to be fulfilled.

l: grace of God, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: The grace of God is sufficient for those who deny themselves of all ungodliness and love God with all their might, mind, and strength. By that grace, they may be perfect and sanctified in Christ.

l: sins, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Those who do away with the things Moroni teaches and die do so in their sins and cannot be saved in the kingdom of God. Through the grace of God and the shedding of the blood of Christ, people may receive remission of their sins and become holy.

l: blood of Christ, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: The blood of Christ is shed in the covenant of the Father for the remission of sins. Through it, people may become holy and without spot.

l: remission of sins, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Remission of sins comes through the shedding of the blood of Christ in the covenant of the Father, allowing people to become holy and without spot.

l: resurrection, The Book of Moroni, Chapter 10
s: Moroni says that his spirit and body will again reunite, and he will be brought forth triumphantly through the air to meet others before the pleasing bar of the great Jehovah.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: This record summarizes the First Book of Nephi, centered on Lehi’s family, Sariah and their sons Laman, Lemuel, Sam, and Nephi, and Nephi’s account of their departure from Jerusalem, journey, and teachings. Lehi receives visions, warns the Jews of Jerusalem’s destruction, and is threatened for prophesying. Commanded by the Lord, he leaves his possessions and leads his family into the wilderness. Nephi is repeatedly portrayed as faithful, while Laman and Lemuel often murmur and rebel. The family returns to Jerusalem twice: first, Nephi and his brothers obtain the plates of brass from Laban after Nephi kills Laban by command and brings Zoram with them; then they bring Ishmael’s family so the sons may take wives. Lehi examines the plates, teaches and prophesies, and recounts a symbolic dream of a tree, iron rod, river, darkness, and great building. Nephi receives related visions of the love of God, the Messiah’s life and death, the apostles, his descendants, Gentiles, Israel’s scattering and gathering, and future records restoring plain and precious parts of the gospel. In the wilderness, the family is guided according to faith, faces hunger and rebellion, and is sustained after Nephi makes a new bow and finds food. At Bountiful, Nephi builds a ship despite his brethren’s opposition. During the sea journey, they bind him, the compass stops, and a storm arises; when freed, Nephi prays and the family reaches the promised land, where they find abundance. Nephi then explains his record-making and teaches from the plates of brass, including writings concerning the God of Israel’s rejection, crucifixion, judgments, salvation, and Israel’s future restoration. The closing chapters address Jacob and Israel: condemnation for treachery, promises of redemption from Babylon, comfort and gathering for scattered Israel, salvation reaching the Gentiles, destruction for those opposing Zion, and preservation and final salvation for those who obey God’s commandments and endure to the end.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: A book recounting Lehi’s family leaving Jerusalem, traveling the wilderness, crossing large waters, and arriving in the promised land.

l: the book of the Lamb of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The book of the Lamb of God is a record of the Jews containing the Lord’s covenants, holy prophets’ prophecies, and the gospel’s fulness; though plain and precious things are taken away, later records establish its truth and restore them.

l: Lehi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Lehi is a prophet, visionary man, faithful to the Lord, husband of Sariah, and father of Laman, Lemuel, Sam, Nephi, Jacob, and Joseph. He dwells in Jerusalem all his days until the Lord warns him to depart because he prophesies of the people’s iniquity, Jerusalem’s destruction, and things he has seen and heard; the people mock and seek to destroy him. After praying with all his heart for his people, he sees a pillar of fire, receives visions and a book, and prophesies. Obeying a dream, he leaves Jerusalem with his family, possessions, and tent, travels into the wilderness, builds an altar, gives thanks, and names the river Laman and valley of Lemuel. He sends his sons back for the plates of brass, rejoices at their return, searches them, learns his genealogy as a descendant of Joseph, and prophesies concerning his seed. His dreams and teachings include the tree, rod of iron, fountain, mists of darkness, large and spacious building, the Jews, Messiah, gospel, Gentiles, and the scattering and gathering of the house of Israel. Though he murmurs during famine and is chastened, he receives revelations about the journey and the ball, leads his family onward, receives the command to go into the ship, and has Jacob and Joseph born in the wilderness. Nephi records his father’s record, genealogy, journeyings, and prophecies.

l: Sariah, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Sariah, Lehi’s wife and mother of Nephi and Sam, rejoices at her sons’ return and testifies of protection and command.

l: Laman, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Laman is Lehi’s elder son, elder brother of Nephi and brother of Lemuel, described as a mighty man who commands fifty men. Compared to the continually running river Laman, he repeatedly murmurs, refuses Nephi’s words, and risks being cut off from the Lord’s presence. Chosen to seek records from Laban, he is rejected and threatened; angered, he smites Nephi and doubts deliverance. Later he flees from Nephi disguised as Laban, rebels while traveling, desires Jerusalem, and does not partake of the fruit in Lehi’s dream. During the voyage he helps bind Nephi, then repents and helps free him when a storm threatens destruction.

l: Lemuel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Lemuel is Lehi’s elder son and Nephi’s elder brother, likened to the firm, steadfast valley of Lemuel. He murmurs against Lehi, refuses Nephi’s words, follows Laman, and joins in harsh speech and violence toward younger brothers. He rebels and seeks to return to Jerusalem, does not partake of the fruit in Lehi’s dream, and causes Lehi fear. During the voyage he murmurs and helps bind Nephi, then repents and helps loose him when a storm threatens destruction.

l: Sam, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Sam, Nephi’s elder brother, believes Nephi, returns for Ishmael’s family, and is seen partaking of fruit near the river.

l: Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nephi is a person, son of Lehi, brother of Laman, Lemuel, and Sam, record maker, prophet, ruler, teacher, and keeper of sacred records. Taught in his father’s learning, he writes with his own hand, abridges his father’s record, makes plates, and bears witness that his record is true. Though exceedingly young, he is large in stature, seeks the mysteries and things of God with lowliness of heart, gains great knowledge of God’s goodness and mysteries, and faithfully keeps the Lord’s commandments without murmuring. He believes his father after receiving a manifestation by the Holy Spirit, teaches Sam, and receives promises for faith and obedience. He leads his brothers to Jerusalem for the plates of brass, persists despite opposition, receives strength, enters the city under the Spirit’s direction, kills Laban at the Spirit’s command, takes Laban’s sword, garments, and armor, obtains the plates, and brings Zoram into the wilderness. He later returns for Ishmael’s family, confronts rebellion among his brethren, and records Lehi’s dream. Seeking to know what his father saw, he receives a vision of the Lamb of God’s ministry and suffering, the future of his seed and his brethren’s seed, nations, kingdoms, Gentiles, the great and abominable church, and the book of the Lamb; he is forbidden to write all he saw and heard. He teaches, preaches diligently, explains scripture and prophecy, and likens scripture for his people’s profit and learning. When his steel bow breaks, he makes a wooden bow, follows the compass, and obtains food. In Bountiful he is instructed to build a ship, makes it as shown by the Lord, guides it to the promised land, and prays during a storm after his brethren bind him. He then makes plates of ore, records sacred things, and teaches his people and brethren from the plates of brass about the Lord, scattering and gathering, destruction of the wicked, and preservation and salvation of the righteous.

l: Ishmael, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Ishmael, father of a family and daughters, gains favor with Nephi, takes his household into the wilderness, later joins opposition to Nephi, travels on, and dies at Nahom.

l: the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The Lord is a deity, God, Redeemer, Savior, Holy One of Israel, and the everlasting God. He is all-powerful, the first and the last, founder of the earth, and one who spans the heavens. He warns Lehi of danger, speaks to him in dreams, accepts his offering, and commands his family to leave Jerusalem for the wilderness. He gives promises of prosperity, authority, and a land of promise to those who keep his commandments. He directs Nephi and his brothers to return for records, favors Nephi for faithfulness, prepares ways for commandments to be fulfilled, protects the family, delivers Laban into Nephi’s hands, and leads them toward the promised land. He provides food, light, provisions, a compass, strength, and guidance; commands and teaches Nephi to build a ship; answers prayer; and calms the storm. He raises up a Messiah, reveals and brings the gospel, and has power to fulfill his words. He made covenants concerning blessings to all kindreds, teaches and leads his people, refines them through affliction, redeems Jacob, and acts against Babylon and the Chaldeans. He comforts, gathers, preserves, restores, and saves Israel; contends with oppressors; raises up a mighty nation among the Gentiles; makes bare his arm to all nations; preserves the righteous; and destroys those who fight against Zion or oppress his people.

l: the Jews, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The Jews are a group within the house of Israel. They mock Lehi for his testimony, seek his life, and are described as wicked. They are taught to be destroyed, carried captive into Babylon, and later returned to their inheritance. They dwindle in unbelief, reject the Lord, and slay the Messiah, then are scattered by the Gentiles. From them proceeds the book of the Lamb of God, which first goes forth in purity through the twelve apostles. In the latter days they are restored so they will not be confounded or scattered again.

l: the people of Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The people of Jerusalem are marked by iniquity, seek to destroy Lehi after his prophecies, and receive warnings from many prophets, including Lehi, to repent or Jerusalem would be destroyed.

l: Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Jerusalem is a great city and land inhabited by its people and the house of Israel, with walls and the house of Laban. It is the place from which Lehi and his family depart, and to which Nephi and his brethren return for the records, later entering by night to obtain the plates of brass and leaving with Zoram. It also is where the God of Israel is crucified. Its central fate is destruction because of the wickedness, abominations, and rejection of prophets by its inhabitants, unless they repent. Its people face death by the sword, captivity into Babylon, scourging, wandering, and becoming a hiss and byword. After captivity, the Jews will return and possess the land of their inheritance.

l: the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The wilderness is a place of travel for Lehi’s family after they leave Jerusalem, containing the valley of Lemuel, the Red Sea, and eventually the land of Bountiful. Lehi is commanded to take his family there, traveling three days before camping in a valley by a river. Nephi and his brothers repeatedly journey, flee, hide, and return through it, including with Zoram and the plates of brass. Over many days and eight years, the family travels nearly eastward toward the land of promise, enduring hunger, sufferings, afflictions, and raw meat. They follow the ball, hunt, and receive fruit, wild honey, beasts, and ore, before reaching large waters and leaving the wilderness for the promised land.

l: the land of Bountiful, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Bountiful is a place reached by Lehi’s family after years in the wilderness. Named for its abundant fruit and wild honey, it lies by the seashore, where the family pitches tents and prepares to build a ship before crossing the large waters.

l: the large waters, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The large waters are reached by Lehi’s family after their travels in the wilderness. The family crosses them into the promised land.

l: the promised land, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The promised land is a land of promise and inheritance, choice above all other lands, reached by Lehi’s family after crossing the large waters. Covenanted to the seed of Nephi’s father, it is later obtained by Gentiles who prosper there; those who hearken to the Lamb may be blessed upon it forever. On arrival, the family settles, plants seeds, and finds abundance.

l: the record of the Jews, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_sought_by Nephi and his brethren's return to Jerusalem The record of the Jews is obtained from the land of Jerusalem after Nephi and his brethren return there.

l: the ship, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The ship, built by Nephi from timbers of curious workmanship according to the Lord’s instructions after his brethren rebel, carries the family, their provisions, seeds, wives, and children across the large waters toward the promised land.

l: the daughters of Ishmael, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Ishmael’s daughters travel in the wilderness, mourn Ishmael’s death, murmur against Nephi’s father and Nephi, and desire to return to Jerusalem; one is Nephi’s wife.

l: Lehi's family, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Lehi’s family is a family including Lehi, Sariah, Laman, Lemuel, Sam, and Nephi. They depart Jerusalem with provisions and tents, travel through the wilderness, rejoice and offer sacrifice after records return, journey with Ishmael’s family, gather seeds, take Ishmael’s daughters as wives, cross large waters, and reach the promised land.

l: Lehi's departure from Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Lehi’s departure is a departure from Jerusalem into the wilderness. Warned by the Lord after prophesying of the people’s iniquity and facing threats to his life, Lehi is commanded in a dream to take his family, provisions, and tents, leaving possessions behind.

l: Lehi's prophecy concerning the people's iniquity, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_about the people's iniquity Lehi’s prophecy concerns the iniquity of the people of Jerusalem. After he prophesies, they seek to destroy his life.

l: the people's iniquity, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The people’s iniquity is the subject of Lehi’s prophecy and the reason the Lord warns him to depart from Jerusalem.

l: the three days' journey into the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: A three-days’ journey into the wilderness, begun after the Lord commands Nephi’s father to depart. Lehi takes his family from Jerusalem along borders near the Red Sea; after three days he pitches his tent in a valley beside a river. Later the family gathers provisions and seed, crosses the river Laman, follows the ball, and travels many days.

l: return to Jerusalem for the records, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: A return to Jerusalem in which Nephi and his brethren seek the record of the Jews, obtain the plates of brass, and bring them to Lehi’s family, who find them desirable and of great worth.

l: the family's sufferings and afflictions in the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Lehi’s family suffers afflictions while traveling in the wilderness.

l: the marriages to the daughters of Ishmael, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: A marriage event in which Lehi’s sons take the daughters of Ishmael as wives.

l: Nephi's brethren's rebellion, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nephi’s brethren rebel against Nephi after the family comes to the large waters. Nephi confounds them, and rebellion against the Lord results in their being cut off from the presence of the Lord, with a sore curse possible.

l: Nephi's shipbuilding, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nephi’s shipbuilding culminates after he confounds his brethren’s rebellion, producing a ship.

l: the crossing of the large waters, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: A crossing in which Lehi’s family travels by ship across the large waters and reaches the promised land.

l: Nephi's record, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nephi’s record, written by Nephi in his father’s language with Jewish learning and Egyptian language, abridges Lehi’s record. It recounts Lehi and his family’s travels and sufferings, shipbuilding, and crossing into the promised land.

l: the Holy One of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The Holy One of Israel is the Messiah, Savior of the world, Redeemer, Lamb of God, Son of God, and a God: the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He redeems children of men from their lost and fallen state, shows them loving kindness, and his doctrine is necessary for salvation. His coming is plainly manifested: he comes to earth, is baptized in Jordan at Bethabara, witnessed by the Holy Ghost as a dove, ministers in power and glory, and heals sickness, affliction, devils, and unclean spirits. Wicked men reject, scourge, smite, spit upon, judge, trample, and crucify him; he is buried in a sepulchre and rises from the dead. Afterward he manifests himself to Gentiles by the Holy Ghost and his gospel comes to Gentiles and the remnant. He preserves Nephi's people, remembers covenants, visits and gathers the house of Israel, numbers and feeds his sheep, executes righteous judgment, and reigns in dominion, might, power, and great glory.

l: prophets, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: prophesy the destruction of Jerusalem [to the people] Prophets of old were shown things concerning Jerusalem, the house of Israel, and Nephi’s people. Their writings are preserved on the plates of brass.

l: Babylon, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: has_as_associated_people Chaldeans Babylon is the place from which Jacob is commanded to go forth and flee. The Lord will do his pleasure on Babylon.

l: the book, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: A book given to Lehi by a heavenly figure commands reading and testifies of Jerusalem’s destruction, the Messiah’s coming, and the world’s redemption.

l: the mysteries of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: are_known_by Nephi [with great knowledge] Nephi states that he had great knowledge of the goodness and the mysteries of God.

l: Lehi's visions and dreams, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: are_written_in the record [many things which Lehi saw] Lehi saw visions and dreams that included a pillar of fire, the heavens opening, God upon His throne, angels, and a descending figure. He also saw and heard many things that he later declared to the people.

l: the destruction of Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The destruction of Jerusalem is a prophesied, certain event. Many prophets, Lehi, and Nephi foretell that, after the people reject prophets and seek Lehi’s life, the Spirit ceases to strive with them; inhabitants perish by the sword and are carried captive into Babylon.

l: Lehi's prayer, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_a prayer [offered in behalf of his people] Lehi prayed to the Lord with all his heart in behalf of his people. During his prayer, a pillar of fire came and dwelt upon a rock before him.

l: the coming of the Messiah, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_manifested_by the book [plainly] Lehi's testimony and the contents of the book manifested plainly the coming of the Messiah.

l: the redemption of the world, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_manifested_by the book [plainly] Lehi's testimony and the contents of the book manifested plainly the redemption of the world.

l: the tender mercies of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: are_over the people of Jerusalem [over all those whom the Lord has chosen because of their faith] Nephi declares that the tender mercies of the Lord are over all those whom the Lord has chosen because of their faith.

l: faith, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Faith is a virtue of diligent seeking and lowliness of heart that brings the Lord’s tender mercies, blessings, revelation, and power of deliverance. It begins as the reason chosen people are delivered, appears in Lehi and Nephi’s faithful actions, and culminates in faith in the Son and Lamb of God enabling revelation and making the twelve ministers’ garments white.

l: the power of deliverance, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: makes the people of Jerusalem [mighty through faith] Nephi states that the Lord's tender mercies can make those chosen because of their faith mighty even unto the power of deliverance.

l: Laman and Lemuel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Laman and Lemuel are Nephi’s brethren, portrayed as stiffnecked murmurers who resist their father, Nephi, and the Lord’s instructions. They leave Jerusalem resentfully, doubt its destruction, and refuse to hearken until confounded. They dispute, fail to inquire, suffer famine, and are chastened for anger and murmuring. They doubt Nephi can build a ship, are shaken by the Lord, bind Nephi during the voyage, then repent when a storm threatens destruction. Later they ask about the plates of brass and are taught their prophecies concern spiritual and temporal things.

l: Lehi's seed, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_a seed [of Nephi] Lehi's seed is promised protection from the power of Laman and Lemuel's seed unless Lehi's seed rebels against the Lord. If they rebel, Laman and Lemuel's seed will be a scourge to stir them up in the ways of remembrance.

l: the Red Sea, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_a sea The Red Sea is near the borders where Lehi travels in the wilderness. The river Laman empties into it, and the valley is near the mouth of the river.

l: the valley of Lemuel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The valley of Lemuel is a valley near the Red Sea, at the mouth of the river Laman. After three days in the wilderness, Lehi pitches his tent there; it becomes where Nephi's father dwells during marriages and the command to journey, and an image of steadfast commandment-keeping.

l: the river Laman, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: River of water beside which Lehi pitches his tent; it empties into the Red Sea and is named as a model for Laman’s righteousness.

l: land of promise, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The land of promise is a land prepared by the Lord for Nephi, promised to Lehi's family, and choice above all other lands. Lehi obtains it and rejoices, while Nephi teaches that faithfulness and keeping the commandments allow people to obtain it. It becomes the setting for multitudes, wars, generations, judgments, and destruction through earthquakes, darkness, fire, sinking cities, and broken mountains and plains.

l: the Spirit and power of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The Spirit and power of God leads Nephi without advance knowledge, commands him concerning Laban, and gives him authority to speak. As the Holy Ghost, it is God’s gift to diligent seekers, comes upon the Messiah as a dove and bears record of him, then falls upon twelve chosen to minister to Nephi’s seed.

l: the dream, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: In a dream, the Lord speaks to Lehi, blesses him for his faithfulness, warns that people seek his life, and commands him to take his family into the wilderness.

l: the commandments of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The commandments of the Lord are directives to be kept with faithfulness and diligence. They ground Lehi’s obedience and guide Nephi, his brethren, and Nephi’s seed. Keeping them brings prosperity in the land of promise, knowledge, nourishment, strength, and means to accomplish what is commanded; rebellion brings separation from the presence of the Lord and other consequences. They lead Nephi and his brothers back to Jerusalem to obtain the plates of brass, which preserve them for children. Across the records, Nephi repeatedly teaches that the Lord prepares a way to fulfill every commandment and exhorts his brethren and later seed to keep them.

l: murmuring, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_a complaint [against one's father] Murmuring is done by Laman and Lemuel against their father. They murmur because they do not understand the dealings of the God who created them and resent leaving Jerusalem and their possessions.

l: the curse, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_a sore curse [upon those who rebel against the Lord] The Lord declares that a sore curse will come upon those who rebel against him. The curse includes having no power over Lehi's seed unless Lehi's seed also rebels against the Lord.

l: Nephi's brothers, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nephi’s younger brothers, outside Jerusalem, murmur over returning for Laban’s records. They try to obtain them with valuables, lose their property, flee, and angrily smite Nephi and other younger brothers. Still angry and murmuring, they follow Nephi to Jerusalem, flee from him, return when called, and depart into the wilderness.

l: Laban, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Laban, a mighty man, possesses the records on the plates of brass. He refuses requests for them, takes property, seeks Nephi’s life, and sends servants against Nephi and his brothers. Found drunk outside his house in Jerusalem, he is delivered into Nephi’s hands and killed with his own sword; Nephi takes his sword, garments, and armor.

l: the plates of brass, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The plates of brass are records of great worth to Lehi’s family. They contain the genealogy of Nephi’s and Lehi’s fathers; the language of Nephi’s fathers; the law of Moses and the five books of Moses; the creation of the world; a record of the Jews from the beginning to the reign of Zedekiah; covenants of the Lord; and writings and prophecies of holy prophets, including Isaiah and Jeremiah. Nephi’s father commands his sons to obtain them so their language and the prophets’ words can be preserved for their children. Nephi obtains the plates from Laban and carries them out of Jerusalem. They testify that prophecies are true and that people must obey God’s commandments. Lehi prophesies they will go to his seed among all nations, kindreds, tongues, and people, and never perish or be dimmed by time.

l: the angel of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: A messenger of the Lord appears as Laman and Lemuel smite Nephi, rebukes them, declares Nephi chosen to rule, promises Laban’s delivery, and departs.

l: Zoram, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Zoram, Laban’s servant and keeper of the treasury keys, mistakes Nephi for Laban and leads him to the plates of brass. In the wilderness, he agrees to go with Nephi’s father and swears to remain with Nephi and his brethren.

l: the law of Moses, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_required_for commandments of the Lord [for keeping them according to the law] Nephi thinks that his people cannot keep the commandments of the Lord according to the law of Moses unless they have the law. He knows that the law is engraved on the plates of brass.

l: Laban's sword, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Laban’s sword, with pure gold hilt and precious steel blade, is drawn by Nephi to kill Laban and impersonate him.

l: Nephi's flight into the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_concealed_from Jews [to prevent pursuit and destruction] Nephi’s flight into the wilderness is intended to take his brethren, the plates of brass, and Zoram away from Jerusalem. Nephi and his brethren fear that the Jews might learn of their flight, pursue them, and destroy them.

l: Laban's death, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_better_than nation's perishing [when the nation would otherwise dwindle and perish in unbelief] Laban’s death occurs after the Spirit commands Nephi to slay him. Nephi takes Laban by the hair and cuts off his head with Laban’s own sword so that he can obtain the plates of brass.

l: oath of Zoram, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: binds Zoram [to remain with Nephi and his brethren] Zoram makes an oath to go into the wilderness with Nephi and his brethren and to remain with them from that time forth. After he makes the oath, their fears concerning him cease.

l: Ishmael's family, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Ishmael’s family travels from Jerusalem into the wilderness with Nephi and his brothers. Some members rebel during the journey, while others plead for Nephi’s life and help soften the rebels’ hearts.

l: the seed of Lehi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Lehi prophesies that the plates of brass will go forth to the nations, kindreds, tongues, and people who are of his seed. He also sees that Nephi and Sam, and many of their seed, will be saved.

l: the land of inheritance, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_location_of a mighty nation [raised up among the Gentiles] This land is the place where the Lord God will raise up a mighty nation among the Gentiles. Blood, fire, and vapor of smoke must come upon its face if people harden their hearts.

l: Lehi's dream, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Lehi's dream is a vision of a dark wilderness containing a desirable tree of life, river, iron rod, narrow path, mist, and spacious building; it brings joy for Nephi and Sam and fear for Laman and Lemuel.

l: the river of water, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The river of water runs near the tree of life and begins where Sariah, Sam, and Nephi stand. In Lehi’s dream, many drown in its depths and others are lost on strange roads. Also called the fountain of filthy water, it represents the depths of hell, filthiness, and an awful gulf separating the wicked from the tree of life and the saints of God.

l: the tree of life, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The tree of life stands in a large and spacious field, bearing fruit desirable to make one happy. Lehi partakes and wants his family to partake. Shown to Nephi as beautiful and white beyond comparison, it represents the love of God and connects with the fountain of living waters. Its fruit is most precious and the greatest of God’s gifts.

l: the fruit of the tree, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The fruit of the tree is sweet, white, and desirable above all other fruit. It is the love of God, filling the soul with exceedingly great joy. Lehi tastes it, and Nephi is shown the tree; those who partake rejoice, though some become ashamed when mocked.

l: the rod of iron, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The rod of iron extends along the bank of the river and leads to the tree of life. In Lehi’s dream, those who cling to it press through the mist of darkness to partake of the tree’s fruit. It represents the word of God, leading to the fountain of living waters or the tree of life; those who hearken and hold fast will not perish or be overcome by the adversary.

l: the strait and narrow path, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: leads_to the tree of life (Lehi's vision) [by the rod of iron] In Lehi’s dream, the strait and narrow path leads to the tree and passes by the head of the fountain toward a large and spacious field. Some who begin on the path lose their way when the mist of darkness arises.

l: the great and spacious building, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: A building high above the earth, filled with finely dressed people who mock those partaking of the fruit. It is the pride of the world and the vain imaginations and pride of the children of men; its mocking causes shame and falling away, before it falls in exceedingly great destruction.

l: the mist of darkness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: In Lehi’s dream, an exceedingly great mist of darkness causes people on the path to lose their way, though some pass through while clinging to the rod of iron. It represents temptations of the devil that blind eyes, harden hearts, and lead people onto broad roads where they perish and are lost.

l: the land of promise journey, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nephi records the journeyings of his family in the wilderness on the plates of ore and the first plates.

l: the angel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: prepares_the_way_for Jesus Christ An angel shows Nephi the virgin, the Son of God, the Messiah’s ministry and suffering, the future of Nephi’s seed, and the meanings of the symbols from Lehi’s vision. The angel explains the fountain, mists of darkness, large and spacious building, and the twelve ministers.

l: the Gentiles, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The Gentiles are many nations and kingdoms separated from the seed of Nephi’s brethren by many waters. They go forth out of captivity, obtain the promised land as an inheritance, become white and exceedingly fair and beautiful, and are lifted above other nations by the power of God. They receive the book of the Lamb of God from the Jews through the twelve apostles, then receive the gospel of the Messiah in the latter days, including its fulness. Their central role is to help graft in the natural branches of the olive-tree and bring the remnants of the house of Israel to knowledge of the true Messiah. Given the servant of the Lord as a light, they are set up as a standard and bring the sons of Israel in their arms. If they hearken unto the Lamb and do not harden their hearts, they can be numbered among the house of Israel; if they repent not, they must perish.

l: the house of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The house of Israel is a people, also called Israel and including a remnant, bound to the covenants of the Lord. It is portrayed as coming forth from Judah and baptism, yet swearing by the Lord without truth or righteousness and becoming obstinate, treacherous, and transgressive. Led by the Lord from bondage through the wilderness and fed with manna, it is compared by the Spirit of the Lord to an olive-tree. Because of wickedness, including that of its pastors, branches are broken off and its people are scattered abroad over all the earth and among the nations, where they are hated because of the Holy One of Israel. The Lord nevertheless remembers them, engraves them on the palms of his hands, and promises their children gathering, deliverance, and salvation. After Gentiles receive the fulness of the Gospel, natural branches are grafted in again; Gentiles who hearken to the Lamb of God may also be numbered among the house. Judgment and mercy follow righteousness or rejection, but when its people cease turning aside their hearts, the Lord remembers his covenants, gathers them from the four quarters to their inherited lands, and restores them. They come to know Jesus Christ, the Holy One of Israel, as true Messiah, Lord, Savior, and Redeemer, dwelling in one fold with one shepherd.

l: the children of men, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The children of men will experience the consequences of hardening their hearts against the Holy One of Israel. Satan will lose power over their hearts when the people dwell in righteousness.

l: the twelve apostles of the Lamb, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The twelve apostles of the Lamb follow the Lamb amid opposition from the multitude of the earth and shall judge the twelve tribes of Israel. They bear record of truth in the Lamb of God, carry the book from the Jews unto the Gentiles, and their record will be established with the records of Nephi's seed.

l: twelve ministers of Nephi's seed, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Twelve ministers of Nephi’s seed are chosen and ordained by God, become righteous through faith in the Lamb of God, and judge Nephi’s seed.

l: seed of Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_overpowered_by seed of Lehi's brethren [because of pride and temptations of the devil] Nephi’s seed experiences wars and contentions, gathers against the seed of his brethren, and is overcome because of its pride and the temptations of the devil. The people of Nephi’s seed are eventually overpowered and many generations pass away.

l: the seed of Nephi's brethren, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The seed of Nephi’s brethren contends with and overpowers Nephi’s seed, then goes forth in multitudes in the land of promise amid wars. It dwindles in unbelief and becomes corrupt. Separated from, scattered, and smitten by Gentiles, it is not utterly destroyed; records come to its remnant.

l: Nazareth, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nazareth is the city where Nephi sees a virgin who is exceedingly fair and white.

l: plates of Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The plates of Nephi preserve Nephi’s people’s ministry, prophecies, instruction, and a greater account of wars, contentions, and destructions. They are kept for instruction and wise purposes and handed down from generation to generation, or prophet to prophet, until further commandments of the Lord.

l: account of the ministry of Nephi's people, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nephi engraves the record of his people on the plates of ore, including his father’s record, their journeyings in the wilderness, and many of his own prophecies.

l: love of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_desirable_above all things [and joyous to the soul] The love of God is represented by the tree of life and the waters of the fountain of living waters. It sheds itself abroad in the hearts of the children of men and is desirable above all things and joyous to the soul.

l: the gospel of the Messiah, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The gospel of the Messiah begins in purity as it goes from the Jews, but the great and abominable church removes many plain and precious parts. Its fulness later comes to the Gentiles, then from them to the remnant of the seed and to those of the house of Israel. It teaches the Redeemer, his doctrine, his rock, and salvation, enabling people to come unto him and be saved. In the end, natural branches are grafted in, know the true Messiah, and the Lord makes bare his arm among the nations.

l: repentance, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Repentance is required to come unto Jesus Christ, brings well-being to repentant Gentiles, and distinguishes those who join Israel from those who perish.

l: sin, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: prevents children of men [from dwelling with God when they remain unclean] The Lamb of God takes away the sins of the world. Those who are in a lost and fallen state must rely on the Redeemer.

l: judgment, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_based_on sin [before God] Every person will be brought into judgment. Those who have sought to do wickedly are unclean before the judgment-seat of God and cannot dwell with God.

l: baptism of the Messiah, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: An angel performs a water baptism as a prophet prepares the Messiah; heavens open and the Holy Ghost descends as a dove.

l: crucifixion of Jesus Christ, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The Lamb of God, the God of Israel, is taken, judged, lifted up on the cross, and crucified for the sins of the world; Jerusalem faces judgment for crucifying him.

l: resurrection of Jesus Christ, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: follows crucifixion of Jesus Christ [after Jesus Christ was slain] After the Messiah is slain, he rises from the dead and makes himself manifest by the Holy Ghost unto the Gentiles.

l: the scattering of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The scattering of Israel is an event in which the house of Israel is dispersed among all nations and across the earth, likened to olive-tree branches broken off. Caused through the Gentiles before latter-day restoration, it follows many hardening their hearts against the Holy One of Israel and precedes grafting in and restoration.

l: gathering of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The gathering of Israel is the latter-days restoration that follows the scattering of the house of Israel. After being broken off, driven out, and scattered because of wickedness, its remnants are gathered from the four quarters of the earth, including the isles of the sea. Natural branches are grafted in after unbelief and the fulness of the gospel through the Gentiles. The people return to Zion, inherit desolate places, are delivered from oppressors, and come out of captivity, obscurity, and darkness to know the Lord as Savior, Redeemer, and the true Messiah.

l: wars among Nephi's people, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nephi sees multitudes of his people gathered to battle, with wars, rumors of wars, great slaughters, and many generations passing away in wars and contentions.

l: destruction of the land of promise, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The land of promise suffers great judgments, including darkness, lightnings, thunderings, earthquakes, broken rocks and plains, sinking cities, burning cities, and tumbling mountains.

l: pride of the world, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The large and spacious building represents the pride of the world. It falls with an exceedingly great fall.

l: temptations of the devil, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The temptations of the devil are represented by the mists of darkness. They blind eyes, harden hearts, and lead people away into broad roads where they perish and are lost.

l: the devil, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The devil founds the great and abominable church and tempts people, blinding their eyes and hardening their hearts. He leads souls into broad roads, captivity, destruction, hell, perishing, and loss.

l: unbelief, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: causes seed of Lehi's brethren [to become dark, loathsome, filthy, and idle] The Jews dwindle in unbelief, and the seed of Nephi’s brethren also dwindles in unbelief. That seed becomes dark, loathsome, filthy, idle, and full of abominations.

l: John, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: John, one of the twelve apostles of the Lamb, sees and writes the remaining things shown, including matters concerning the end of the world.

l: the Lamb of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The Lamb of God is the Son of the Eternal Father and Savior of the world. He brings forth much of his gospel, manifests himself to Gentiles and Jews, and establishes his words through records.

l: remnant of the house of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: A remnant and broken-off branch of the house of Israel, scattered by nations through a mighty Gentile nation. Its seed is judged and smitten, later receives further records, and may include Gentiles who hearken to the Lamb of God; the marvelous work is of great worth to it.

l: the great and abominable church, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The great and abominable church, founded by the devil and called the mother of harlots and whore of all the earth, slays, tortures, binds, and captivates saints. Desiring gold and silver, it removes plain and precious gospel parts and covenants, perverts the Lord’s ways, and gathers multitudes against the Lamb. It ultimately turns upon its own head, tumbles to dust, and suffers a great fall.

l: the church of the Lamb of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The church of the Lamb of God consists of the saints of God across the earth, yet has few numbers and dominions because of the wickedness and abominations of the whore; its members receive the Lamb’s power and are armed with righteousness and God’s power.

l: the covenants of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The covenants of the Lord concern the house of Israel: promises made with its fathers, including Abraham’s seed blessing all kindreds of the earth. They address Israel’s scattering and later gathering, are contained in the book of the Lamb of God, and will be fulfilled and made known despite many being taken away. When Israel no longer turns aside, the Lord will remember them.

l: the marvelous work among the Gentiles, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: A great and marvelous work among the Gentiles and children of men, performed after Nephi's seed is scattered. It makes the Lord's covenants known to all Israel and nourishes Israel. Greatly valuable to Nephi's seed and the Gentiles, it leads to peace and eternal life or to hardness, blindness, captivity, and destruction.

l: captivity, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_caused_by the devil The Gentiles go forth out of captivity upon the many waters and are delivered by the power of God from other nations. The devil seeks to bring souls into captivity, while those who hearken to the Lamb will be no more brought down into captivity.

l: wars among the nations, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: occur_among all the nations and kindreds of the earth [when the wrath of God is poured out upon the great and abominable church] Wars and rumors of wars arise among all the nations belonging to the mother of abominations. These events occur as the wrath of God is poured out upon the great and abominable church.

l: the wrath of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The wrath of God is upon Nephi's brethren's seed, scattered and smitten before Gentiles, and is poured upon those gathered against Gentiles and the great church.

l: Isaiah, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_a prophet Isaiah’s writings are read by Nephi to persuade his brethren to believe in the Lord their Redeemer. Nephi likens Isaiah’s words to his people so they may have hope.

l: the remnant of our seed, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The remnant of the seed dwindles in unbelief for many years, then receives the gospel through the Gentiles, is grafted into the true olive-tree, recognizes its place in Israel, and knows its Redeemer.

l: the wicked, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The wicked are separated from the righteous and tree of life by God’s justice; dying in wickedness, they cannot dwell in God’s kingdom, lack peace, burn as stubble, and are cast into hell.

l: the righteous, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The righteous are justified by truth and separated from the wicked through God’s justice. At the last day they are lifted up. Preserved by God’s power through their enemies’ destruction, they need not fear; if they repent, they dwell safely in the Holy One of Israel and are led up as calves of the stall.

l: the kingdom of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_a place where the righteous dwell [no unclean thing enters] The kingdom of God is clean, and no unclean thing can enter it. The wicked cannot dwell there if their works are filthy.

l: hell, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_a place of filthiness [prepared for the wicked] Hell is prepared for the wicked and is the place to which those rejected from the righteous and the tree of life are cast.

l: the olive-tree, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: represents the house of Israel [in the prophetic comparison] The olive-tree represents the house of Israel. Natural branches are broken off and later grafted into the true olive-tree.

l: the natural branches, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: are_grafted_into the true olive-tree [in the latter days] The natural branches represent the remnant of Israel. They are scattered by the Gentiles and are later grafted into the true olive-tree.

l: the word of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The word of God is represented by the rod of iron and has almighty power over the earth and its conditions. It protects, leads, feeds, and delivers those who heed it, hold fast, and keep the commandments; those who harden their hearts after hearing it become past feeling.

l: the ball, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: A round fine-brass ball contains two spindles and written directions, pointing the way through the wilderness; its pointers and writing work and change according to the family's faith, diligence, and heed.

l: Nephi's bow, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_a bow [made of fine steel] Nephi's bow is made of fine steel and breaks while he is hunting for food. Its loss contributes to the family's famine, after which Nephi makes a new bow from wood.

l: the covenant with Abraham, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: promises blessings to all kindreds of the earth [through Abraham's seed] The covenant with Abraham promises that all the kindreds of the earth will be blessed through Abraham's seed. Nephi identifies it as the covenant to be fulfilled in the latter days.

l: the restoration of the Jews, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: occurs_in the latter days [after which they are no more scattered] The restoration of the Jews will occur in the latter days. After being restored, the Jews will no more be confounded or scattered again.

l: Ishmael's death, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: occurs_in Nahom [where Ishmael is buried] Ishmael's death occurs at Nahom during the family's journey in the wilderness. His daughters mourn and then murmur against Nephi's father and Nephi.

l: the judgment of mankind, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The judgment of mankind judges wicked and righteous people according to their works, including probationary temporal works; the filthy cannot enter God’s kingdom.

l: faith and diligence, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: determines the operation of the ball [with heed] Faith and diligence affect whether the ball's pointers work and what is written upon it. The writing changes according to the faith and diligence given to it.

l: murmuring against the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_a sin [requiring chastening and repentance] Murmuring against the Lord occurs after Nephi's bow breaks and the family suffers from hunger. The Lord chastens the murmurers, who turn away their anger and repent.

l: Nephi's preaching, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: causes the brethren's humility [before the Lord] Nephi preaches to his brethren about the house of Israel, the restoration of the Jews, the meaning of his father's dream, the judgment of mankind, and the need to keep the commandments.

l: the famine in the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: causes suffering [through lack of food] The famine in the wilderness follows the breaking of Nephi's bow and the loss of the other bows' springs. The family suffers hunger until Nephi obtains food by using his new bow.

l: the written directions on the ball, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: give understanding [concerning the ways of the Lord] The written directions on the ball give understanding concerning the ways of the Lord and guide the family through the wilderness. The writing is plain to read and changes according to their faith and diligence.

l: the sea, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_called Irreantum [meaning many waters] The family beholds the sea at Bountiful and calls it Irreantum, meaning many waters. They later cross it in the ship toward the promised land, though a storm drives them back for four days.

l: the compass, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The compass, prepared by the Lord for steering the ship, ceases during Nephi’s binding and works again after his brethren loose him according to his desire.

l: the construction of the ship, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_commanded_by the Lord [to carry the people across the sea] The construction of the ship begins after the Lord commands Nephi to build it and tells him where to find ore. Nephi makes tools, receives repeated instruction from the Lord, and completes workmanship that his brethren recognize as exceedingly fine.

l: the voyage to the promised land, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_guided_by the compass [after Nephi is released] The voyage begins after the family boards the ship with provisions, seeds, and their families. Nephi’s brethren bind him, the compass stops, and the ship is driven backward by a great storm until they repent; afterward Nephi guides the ship to the promised land.

l: the great storm, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: A great and terrible storm, caused after Nephi is bound and the compass ceases to work, drives the ship back four days until Nephi is loosed and prays.

l: Nephi's people, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nephi's people possess promised land, endure wars and destructions, and receive Nephi’s instructive records about the Lord and prophets.

l: plates of ore, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Plates of ore contain Nephi’s people’s record, journeyings, and prophecies, made by commandment and engraved by Nephi.

l: scriptures, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nephi likens all scriptures unto his people for their profit and learning. He reads from the scriptures to persuade them to believe in the Lord their Redeemer.

l: wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: preserves house of Israel [through God of Israel] The wilderness is the setting of the journey of Nephi’s family, and the first plates contain much of their proceedings there.

l: the isles of the sea, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: receive signs and wonders [through three days of darkness] The isles of the sea will receive signs of the God of Israel’s death through three days of darkness. The Lord will remember the isles of the sea and gather the house of Israel.

l: prophecies, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nephi engraves many of his own prophecies and records the prophecies of his father. The prophecies concern the ministry, suffering, death, resurrection-related signs, judgments, covenants, and gathering of Israel.

l: wars, contentions, and destructions, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The other plates give a greater account of the wars, contentions, and destructions of Nephi’s people.

l: making of the plates, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nephi makes the plates by commandment of the Lord so that sacred things may be preserved for the knowledge and instruction of his people.

l: three days of darkness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Three days of darkness will be a sign of the God of Israel’s death, especially for those who inhabit the isles of the sea and those of the house of Israel.

l: salvation, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Salvation is the Lord’s blessing and help, bringing great joy to the righteous among the house of Israel when he visits them. Given through the servant as a light to the Gentiles, it is seen by all earth and extends to its ends.

l: affliction, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_a furnace Affliction is described as a furnace in which the Lord has refined and chosen the house of Jacob.

l: Chaldeans, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The Chaldeans are commanded to be fled from, and the Lord's arm shall come upon them.

l: peace, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_like a river [for those who hearken to the commandments] Peace would have been like a river if the house of Jacob had hearkened to the Lord's commandments. There is no peace, saith the Lord, unto the wicked.

l: Zion, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Zion, believing herself forsaken by the Lord, faces destruction and nations’ attacks; the Lord denies forgetting her, promises her children’s return and renewal, and declares her attackers will be destroyed.

l: servant of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The servant of the Lord is called from the womb, formed and hidden as a sharp sword and polished shaft, then appointed to restore Jacob and Israel, become a light to the Gentiles, a covenant of the people, and salvation to earth’s ends.

l: covenant, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The Lord gives his servant as a covenant for the people, establishing the earth and restoring desolate heritages.

l: redemption, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: is_a deliverance [from captivity and oppression] The Lord identifies himself as the Redeemer of Israel and declares that he will deliver the captives and the prey of the terrible. He will contend with those who contend with his people and save their children.

l: Jesus Christ, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Jesus Christ is not named in this unit.

l: Satan, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Satan has power over hearts until it is removed; during the righteous reign, people’s righteousness leaves him powerless and unable to be loosed for many years.

l: the kingdom of the devil, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The kingdom of the devil is established among those in the flesh, built through churches seeking gain, power, popularity, and worldly lusts; it ends with its members brought low in the dust and consumed as stubble.

l: the nations, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nations war against Israel, then see the Lord God fulfill covenants and gospel; those opposing Israel turn against one another and fall into their own pit.

l: obedience to the commandments of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: leads_to the last day [with endurance to the end] Obedience to the commandments of God is required for salvation at the last day, together with enduring to the end.

l: the destruction of the wicked, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The wicked will be brought low, consumed as stubble, and destroyed. The righteous will be preserved while the enemies of the Lord are destroyed by fire.

l: the reign of the Holy One of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The Holy One of Israel will reign in dominion, might, power, and great glory. During his reign, the gathered people will form one fold with one shepherd.

l: the millennium of righteousness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The millennium of righteousness is not named in this unit.

l: the last day, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Those who are obedient to the commandments of God and endure to the end will be saved at the last day.

l: The Second Book of Nephi
s: These records summarize The Second Book of Nephi, in which Lehi’s final teachings, Nephi’s leadership, Jacob’s sermons, and extensive prophetic writings describe God’s covenants, Christ’s redemption, Israel’s scattering and gathering, and the path to eternal life. Lehi recalls the Lord’s mercy in bringing his family from Jerusalem, warns that obedience brings liberty and prosperity while sin brings captivity, blesses his children, and urges Laman, Lemuel, their families, Zoram, and others to follow Nephi. He teaches that opposition, agency, the Fall, and the Holy Messiah’s atonement make joy, redemption, resurrection, and choice possible. He also recounts prophecies concerning Joseph’s descendants, records, seers, restoration, and the house of Israel. After Lehi dies, conflict intensifies: Nephi’s brothers seek his life, so Nephi leads his family and followers away, establishes the people of Nephi, builds a temple, appoints Jacob and Joseph as priests and teachers, keeps records, and faces wars with the Lamanites. Jacob teaches from Isaiah about Israel’s scattering, the Messiah’s suffering and return, judgment, restoration, and the need to repent and come unto Christ. Isaiah’s words then portray Judah and Jerusalem’s wickedness, desolation, judgment, future purification, a righteous ruler, gathering, deliverance, and joy; they also foretell judgments on Assyria and Babylon and the eventual recovery of Israel. Nephi explains that these prophecies point to Christ, whom he and Jacob have seen, and teaches that the law of Moses typifies him. Nephi further prophesies Christ’s ministry, death, resurrection, appearance to his people, the destruction and later fall of his own people, the rise of false churches and secret combinations, the coming forth of a sealed book and written testimonies, a marvelous work, and the gathering of Israel. He warns against pride, priestcraft, false doctrine, and rejecting further revelation, while affirming that God speaks to many nations and offers salvation freely. The book closes with Nephi’s plain doctrine of Christ: repent, be baptized, receive the Holy Ghost, press forward in faith, feast on Christ’s words, pray, endure to the end, and be reconciled to Christ before final judgment.

l: Lehi, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Lehi is a father and prophet who receives a vision of Jerusalem’s destruction, beholds the Lord’s glory, and prophesies concerning the land of promise and Joseph’s seed. In his final days, he teaches his family about the Lord’s dealings, obedience, rebellion, creation, opposition, the fall, redemption, and choices before men. He urges his sons to unite in righteousness, obey Nephi, and remember the commandments, while blessing Laman’s and Lemuel’s children, Ishmael’s household, Sam, and Zoram. Having chosen the good part and sought their everlasting welfare, he grows old, dies, is buried, and is redeemed from hell.

l: Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Nephi is a brother of Laman, Lemuel, and Sam; a speaker, writer, ruler, teacher, king or protector, and prophet among the people of Nephi. From the family’s departure from Jerusalem, he keeps the Lord’s commandments, seeks God’s glory and his brethren’s eternal welfare, and acts through the power of God. Lehi describes him as helping bring the family through the wilderness and directs his brethren to hearken to him so they will not perish. Nephi records scriptures, the things of his soul, and writings on plates. He delights in scriptures, Isaiah’s words, the Lord’s covenants, grace, justice, power, mercy, and plainness. In sorrow over sin, temptations, afflictions, and enemies, he prays, trusts the Lord forever rather than the arm of flesh, and is supported through afflictions. When his brethren become angry, he flees into the wilderness with believers. He leads, teaches, governs, and protects his people; builds a temple, makes swords, consecrates priests and teachers, and keeps records. He possesses the plates of brass, the ball or compass prepared for his father, and the sword of Laban. He writes Isaiah and teaches plainly about Christ, repentance, baptism, receiving the Holy Ghost, enduring to the end, remission of sins, and obedience to God’s commandments. He prophesies concerning Jews, Gentiles, his seed, Israel, and the Lord’s future work. Near the end, he mourns over unbelief and wickedness, says he is stronger in speaking than writing, continues praying for his people, and writes as commanded, with faith in Christ and charity for his people, the Jews, and the Gentiles.

l: Laman, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Laman, Lehi’s son, receives a blessing that his seed will endure, then rebels against and becomes angry with Nephi after Lehi’s death; he has sons and daughters.

l: Lemuel, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Lemuel, Lehi’s son, rebels against and later grows angry with Nephi; his sons and daughters receive Lehi’s blessing that they and their seed will not be utterly destroyed.

l: Lord God, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Lord God is God, creator of all things, king of heaven, Savior and Redeemer of his covenant people. He has eternal purposes and possesses power, mercy, and justice; he is just, unchanging, works not in darkness, and loves all the world. He creates, gives commandments and law, grants light and understanding, speaks to every people according to their language, hears faithful prayer, and judges the world by what is written and by works. He begins by warning Lehi’s family to flee Jerusalem, bringing them to a promised land, consecrating it for inheritance, and blessing those who keep his commandments. Rejection brings cutting off, cursing, other nations, scattering, captivity, and judgment; repentance brings mercy, salvation, restoration, liberty, and covenant blessings. He deals with Nephi, the Lamanites, Jacob’s children, Gentiles, Jews, Nephites, lost tribes, and all children of men: he remembers covenants, fulfills promises, lifts standards, and will deliver his covenant people. He helps, teaches, justifies, and is near to his servant. He opposes counsels and works against his people, calls them to seek God rather than the dead, and will destroy darkness, murder, and abominations. He brings forth a book and his words through witnesses, gives further words line upon line, and preserves his word. The record ends with Nephi’s faith that Lord God hears and consecrates his prayers for his people.

l: Holy One of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Holy One of Israel is God, the Lord of Israel, who knows all things and gives commandments tied to inheritance, preservation of seed, repentance, baptism, faith, and enduring to the end. He suffers for all men and every living creature in Adam’s family, provides resurrection and atonement, and is the keeper of the gate and only way. He judges people and nations according to his word, delivers the righteous from the devil, death, hell, and endless torment, restores his people, and provides salvation through Jesus Christ. Those who reject his law and word face condemnation; he sends Assyria against a hypocritical nation, then punishes its pride and removes its burden. His work culminates in judgment, restoration, and joy as the poor and meek rejoice in him.

l: Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Jesus Christ is the Holy Messiah, the Only Begotten of the Father, the Son of God, the Eternal God, and the Holy One of Israel. Full of grace and truth, he offers himself as a sacrifice for sin for those with broken hearts and contrite spirits. He lays down his life in the flesh, takes it up by the Spirit’s power, rises first to bring about the resurrection of the dead, redeems souls from hell, and intercedes for all the children of men. Though rejected, scourged, and crucified, he becomes the source of salvation, reconciliation, remission of sins, strength, song, comfort, and healing for the righteous. He manifests himself in the flesh to the house of Israel and to Nephi’s people, gives law, and manifests himself through the Holy Ghost to those who believe. He works miracles among the children of men according to faith, recovers covenant people a second time in power and great glory, preserves believers, and will show at the last day that Nephi’s words are his. His message calls people to believe in him, be reconciled unto him, and endure to the end.

l: Christ, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Christ is the Redeemer, Lamb of God, Son, Lord, Savior, and God who is mighty to save. He is necessary for men, for without his coming all must perish. In the fulness of his own time, he comes among the Jews, who crucify him because of priestcrafts and iniquities. He fulfills righteousness through baptism, obeys God the Father, follows the straight and narrow path, and sets an example for the children of men. He commands them to follow him, gives the Holy Ghost through the Father to those baptized in his name, and teaches that enduring to the end brings salvation. His words tell people what they should do, and he will manifest himself in the flesh. He empowers the reading of the sealed words and the revealing of all things. The scattered house of Israel will be gathered when it comes to know its Redeemer.

l: the devil, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The devil is an angel who fell from heaven and from before the presence of the Eternal God after seeking evil. He is the father of all lies and seeks the misery of all mankind. He beguiled the first parents, nearly transforms himself into an angel of light, and founds secret combinations, murder, and works of darkness. He stirs up children of men to secret works and anger against good, while lulling others into carnal security and flattering them to deny hell. He leads people gradually by a flaxen cord, gains place in the heart, destroys peace, and uses captivity, strong cords, and everlasting chains to make them his prey and bring them down to hell.

l: Jerusalem, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Jerusalem is a holy city and place of origin for Jacob, his people, and Lehi’s family; it is also the source from which the people of Nephi came. Lehi’s family was warned to flee because Jerusalem was destroyed, and those who remained were slain or carried captive, though the Lord showed Jacob they would return. Jerusalem drinks the Lord’s fury, lacks guidance, and is commanded to awake, rise from the dust, clothe itself, and loose its bands. Its people, including the Jews and men of Judah, oppose the Lord through their words and deeds, stiffen their necks against Christ, and are associated with Christ’s crucifixion. The city is ruined, oppressed, desolate, and mourning: its gates lament, and it sits upon the ground. Yet those remaining and written among the living are called holy, and the Lord purges its blood through judgment and burning. Jerusalem faces war but its attackers cannot prevail. It is included in the Lord’s work, is threatened by the Assyrian, and is the place from which the word of the Lord goes forth in the last days. After the Jews return from captivity, Jerusalem is destroyed again after Jesus Christ rises from the dead.

l: land of promise, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The land of promise is choice above all lands, consecrated and kept for those brought there. It is a land of liberty, prosperity, security, and inheritance for the righteous who serve the Lord and keep his commandments; Sam and his seed inherit it like Nephi. If iniquity abounds, it is cursed and people are removed from their possessions.

l: wilderness, The Second Book of Nephi
s: contains the place Nephi The wilderness is where Nephi and those who follow him flee after departing from his brethren. The Lamanites seek in the wilderness for beasts of prey.

l: the earth, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The earth was created by God with the heavens and all things in them, and would not exist without God or creation. It includes a choice land where Jacob’s seed dwells and worships God, and from its four parts and sea isles the Jews will be gathered. The rod and branch smite it, and it becomes full of knowledge of the Lord. In the Lord of Hosts’ fierce anger, it removes from its place as the heavens are shaken. The Lord judges and divides its people, destroys the wicked, and spares his people. At last it is at rest and quiet, sings, and is full of the knowledge of the Lord, with nothing to hurt or destroy in his holy mountain.

l: hell, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Hell is a place beneath heaven identified with spiritual death and the death of the spirit. It holds captive spirits, contains the dead, and is a place of punishment and endless torment. It enlarges itself and opens its mouth without measure as glory, multitude, pomp, and rejoicing descend into it. It moves to meet the king of Babylon, stirring the dead and kings. Though denied by some, it and the devil stand before God’s throne for judgment, while the wicked are sent to endless torment.

l: nations, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Nations are central to promises, judgment, gathering, conflict, and Zion. They may be kept from the land of promise while the people brought from Jerusalem keep commandments, but will overrun it if those people reject the Holy One of Israel. In the last days all nations flow to the mountain of the Lord’s house, where the Lord judges and rebukes them, ending their warfare. The Lord of Hosts summons nations from far by an ensign; they come swiftly prepared for battle and carry away prey. Nations are also ruled by an oppressor, yet receive word that the Lord has founded Zion, where the poor trust.

l: children of men, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The children of men are free to choose eternal life through the great Mediator or eternal death through the devil, and are accountable under law, judgment, and the consequences of those choices. Because of the fall and their parents’ transgression, they are lost, unholy, and subject to death; therefore all must repent. They can receive resurrection and salvation through the Holy One of Israel by believing, repenting, being baptized by water, receiving the Holy Ghost with real intent, keeping God the Father’s commandments, following Jesus Christ, and enduring to the end. According to faith, they receive miracles, signs, wonders, teachings concerning Christ, and God’s goodness. As they receive the word of God and heed precepts and counsel, they gain wisdom, doctrine, and understanding, including those who erred or murmured. The account culminates in further writings and the eventual revelation of all things: secrets are made manifest, works of darkness are exposed, and sealed things upon the earth are loosed.

l: seed of Lehi, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The seed of Lehi is promised an inheritance in the land of promise: keeping commandments brings blessing, prosperity, possession, and safety; rejecting the Holy One of Israel brings God’s judgments, scattering, and loss of lands.

l: the righteous, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The righteous are assured that it is well with them and that they will receive the fruit of their doings. They gain perfect knowledge, purity, and the robe of righteousness, inherit the kingdom of God, and receive justice at judgment. They heed prophets despite persecution, look forward steadfastly to Christ, do not perish, and are healed by Jesus Christ.

l: vision of Jerusalem's destruction, The Second Book of Nephi
s: shows Jerusalem [as destroyed] Lehi says that he saw a vision in which he knew that Jerusalem was destroyed. The vision confirmed that remaining in Jerusalem would have caused his family to perish.

l: departure from Jerusalem, The Second Book of Nephi
s: prevents death [Lehi's family would have perished if they had remained] The departure from Jerusalem occurred because the Lord warned Lehi’s family to flee. Lehi teaches that the Lord brought them into the land of promise and that their preservation came through this departure.

l: rebellion, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Lehi recalls his sons’ rebellions on the waters and says that God spared their lives. He commands them to rebel no more against Nephi, whom they had sought to kill despite his service and faithfulness.

l: journey through the wilderness, The Second Book of Nephi
s: lasts many days Nephi and those with him take their tents and whatever things are possible and journey in the wilderness for many days before pitching their tents.

l: covenant concerning the land, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_made_by the Lord God [with Lehi] The Lord covenants with Lehi that the land will be an inheritance for his seed, his children, and those led there by the Lord. The covenant promises liberty, prosperity, protection, and possession of the land to those who keep the Lord’s commandments.

l: commandments, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Commandments are divine requirements urged by Lehi and taught by the Lord God. Keeping them brings prosperity in the land, blessing, liberty, security, and protection from captivity; refusing them brings separation from God's presence. Jesus Christ keeps them in obedience to God the Father, and his followers must repent, be baptized, and keep the commandments to enter the way to eternal life.

l: law of prosperity and destruction, The Second Book of Nephi
