s: governs land of promise [according to obedience or disobedience] The law states that those who keep the Lord’s commandments will prosper in the land, while those who refuse will be cut off from his presence. Continued iniquity can bring cursing, destruction of soul and body, loss of possessions, scattering, and captivity.

l: liberty, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Liberty, available through the Holy Messiah, leads toward eternal life when chosen and is a condition of the land unto the Gentiles, where no kings raise themselves up.

l: iniquity, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Iniquity is sin and wrongdoing that burdens souls and brings sorrow. It curses the land of inheritance and draws the Lord’s wrath, judgments, conflict, famine, captivity, and destruction. Nephi grieves over his own iniquities and resolves to reject sin. Among nations, Gentiles, and Jews, it brings drunkenness, hidden works, covered rulers and seers, and visitation.

l: unbelief, The Second Book of Nephi
s: causes destruction of the wicked [when combined with pride and works of darkness] Unbelief will cause many of Nephi’s people to dwindle and be destroyed. Those who seek to destroy the things of God will not receive the written records concerning them.

l: judgments of God, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The judgments of God rest upon those who reject the Holy One of Israel after blessings and knowledge, including the seed of Lehi and the people of Nephi. As hearts harden, judgments bring other nations, loss of lands, scattering, smiting, bloodshed, affliction, and visitations. They come upon all nations according to his word; the Jews’ destructions were foretold because of iniquities.

l: scattering and captivity, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Scattering and captivity afflict the seed of Lehi and the Jews as consequences of rejecting the Lord and his commandments. Lehi warns of lost lands, smiting, and devilish captivity; after Jerusalem’s destruction, the Jews are scattered, scourged, and eventually persuaded to believe in Christ.

l: death of Lehi, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_imminent Lehi [a few days before his speech] Lehi says that he will soon lay down his limbs in the cold and silent grave and go the way of all the earth. Before his death, he urges his sons to arise, obey, unite, and avoid bringing him grief and sorrow.

l: faith, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Faith strengthens the word of the Lord through weak words, enables a seer’s work, and empowers one mighty among Joseph’s descendants. Perfect faith in the Holy One of Israel, joined with repentance, baptism, and endurance, is required for salvation and inheriting God’s kingdom. It makes Nephi’s people alive in Jesus Christ and centers their hope under the fulfilled law.

l: the power of God, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The power of God is with Nephi through the Spirit of the Lord, opening his mouth and enabling him to speak boldly and command obedience. It enables faith to do all things. False teachers, churches, and followers deny it and the gift of the Holy Ghost, bringing condemnation.

l: chains of sin, The Second Book of Nephi
s: bind children of men [carrying them captive to misery and woe] Lehi calls on his sons to awake from the sleep of hell and shake off the awful chains that bind the children of men. He identifies these chains with captivity and misery and urges them to put on the armor of righteousness and arise from the dust.

l: lands of promise, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The lands of promise are choice, precious lands of inheritance, consecrated forever to Jacob’s children and Joseph’s seed. They are lands of liberty for the Gentiles and fortified by God. Security depends on keeping commandments; believing Jews are restored, and people return from the ends of the earth.

l: Jacob, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Jacob is Lehi’s first-born in the wilderness and Nephi’s brother. He suffers affliction and sorrow in childhood because of his brethren, knows God’s greatness, beholds Christ in youth, and is redeemed through his Redeemer’s righteousness. Consecrated by Nephi and ordained after God’s holy order, he serves God throughout his days. He speaks to Nephi’s people and beloved brethren, anxiously teaching for their souls’ welfare. He reads and explains Isaiah concerning the house of Israel, teaches of Christ, Jews, Gentiles, God’s promises, and reconciliation to God’s will, and witnesses that he has seen Christ. He receives revelation, word, and mercy from the Lord; the house of Jacob will be joined by strangers and his people brought to their place.

l: Adam, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Adam, first parent with Eve, transgresses by partaking of forbidden fruit, falls from Eden, and makes possible mankind’s probation, knowledge of good and evil, and joy.

l: Eve, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Eve, first parent with Adam, is persuaded by the old serpent to eat forbidden fruit; after they partake, both are driven from Eden to till earth.

l: brethren, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Nephi’s elder brethren grow angry, accuse him of seeking rule, attempt to kill him, refuse his words and leadership, are cut off from the Lord God, and later war with his people.

l: heaven, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Lucifer will fall from heaven after seeking to ascend into it and exalt his throne above the stars of God.

l: the garden of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: contains tree of life [alongside the forbidden fruit] The garden of Eden was where Adam and Eve would have remained if Adam had not transgressed. After partaking of the forbidden fruit, they were driven out to till the earth.

l: the Spirit, The Second Book of Nephi
s: teaches prayer [teaches a man to pray] The Spirit stoppeth Nephi's utterance. The Spirit teaches a man to pray.

l: the resurrection, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The resurrection is brought to pass by the Holy Messiah through his death and rising. It comes because of the fall, raises people from death, restores bodies and spirits to one another, and makes all children of men incorruptible and immortal before judgment.

l: fall of man, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The fall of man came through Adam and Eve’s transgression, bringing mankind out of the garden of Eden, cutting men off from the Lord, and bringing death. In the fulness of time, Holy Messiah redeems the children of men, enabling resurrection and freedom to act.

l: transgression of Adam, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Adam's transgression causes the fall, ending innocence while enabling men's existence, probation, and opportunity for joy.

l: forbidden fruit, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_in_opposition_to tree of life [one sweet and the other bitter] The forbidden fruit stood in opposition to the tree of life. After Adam and Eve partook of it, they were driven out of the garden of Eden and came to know good and evil.

l: law, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The law is given to men to distinguish good from evil, but justifies no flesh. It cuts men off and establishes punishment and condemnation for transgression; without it, neither applies. The Messiah fulfills its ends for the broken and contrite, while atonement claims mercy for those not given it.

l: sin, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Sin is defined by law and opposition, is abhorred by the Holy One of Israel, and is likened to Sodom. It makes people guilty, unclean, spiritually dead, and separated from the Lord; vanity draws it in like a cart rope, so people are called to turn away and come unto God.

l: righteousness, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Righteousness is everlasting and opposed to wickedness, made possible through law and opposition. Believers in the Messiah may be saved through his intercession and righteousness. The Lord seeks it from Judah, sanctifies himself in it, and assures those who follow it that it will remain forever.

l: good and evil, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Men receive sufficient instruction to know good from evil and remain free to act; the condemned nevertheless call evil good.

l: salvation, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Salvation is a free, everlasting gift prepared from the fall of man, available alike to all people and never abolished. No flesh can dwell in God's presence except through the merits, mercy, and grace of the Holy Messiah. A promised seer’s work brings Joseph’s people to it through the Lord’s power. Identified with God, it inspires trust without fear and joy drawn from its wells. The Lord offers it freely and commands persuasion of all men to repentance.

l: redemption, The Second Book of Nephi
s: comes_through Holy Messiah Redemption comes through the Holy Messiah, who offers himself as a sacrifice for sin and makes intercession for mankind. The children of men are redeemed from the fall through him.

l: the atonement, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The atonement is an infinite provision for all mankind, received through the Holy Messiah. It answers the ends of the law and relates to punishment and happiness attached to human choices. Necessary for resurrection, it enables corruption to put on incorruption and prevents the first judgment from continuing endlessly. It satisfies justice for those without the law, delivers them from death and torment, raises people from everlasting death, and may receive them into God’s eternal kingdom.

l: grace of God, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Grace of God is the means by which reconciled people, including Jacob’s brethren and children of men, are saved after all they can do; Jacob and Nephi’s people teach that it invites praise, belief in Christ, and reconciliation with God.

l: opposition, The Second Book of Nephi
s: exists_in all things [as a necessary condition] Opposition is necessary in all things so that righteousness, wickedness, holiness, misery, good, and bad can exist. It existed between the forbidden fruit and the tree of life and enables meaningful choice.

l: the day of probation, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The day of probation may be wasted by transgressors and ends after reconciliation and continued progress in the strait path.

l: agency, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_given_to men [so that man may act for himself] Men are given the ability to act for themselves rather than merely be acted upon. They are enticed by one choice or the other and may choose liberty and eternal life or captivity and death.

l: captivity, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Captivity, chosen through the devil with death, grants devilish power toward hell until the Messiah frees Joseph’s branch.

l: eternal life, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Eternal life is a freely chosen way received through the great Mediator. Men and children of men are instructed to look to the Mediator, obey his commandments, reconcile to the will of God, and rely on grace. The path unfolds through faithfulness, pressing forward in Christ with hope and love, feasting on his word, and enduring to the end, which is identified as eternal life.

l: everlasting death, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Everlasting death is a way chosen by people according to the flesh and evil within them, rejecting God's will. This choice lets the devil captivate and bring them to hell, though God may raise people from it through the atonement.

l: happiness, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_opposed_to misery [as consequences attached to law] Happiness is opposed to punishment and misery and depends on righteousness. Adam's fall made it possible for men to have joy, and the absence of righteousness would mean the absence of happiness.

l: misery, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_sought_for men [by the devil] Misery is opposed to happiness and is associated with wickedness, punishment, and the devil's purposes. The devil seeks that all mankind might be miserable like himself.

l: afflictions, The Second Book of Nephi
s: are_experienced_by Nephi [in the wilderness and elsewhere] The Lord leads Nephi through his afflictions in the wilderness and preserves him upon the waters of the great deep. Nephi asks why his heart should weep, his flesh waste away, or his strength slacken because of afflictions.

l: Joseph (Lehi's last-born son), The Second Book of Nephi
s: Joseph, Lehi's last-born son, is born in the wilderness during Lehi's greatest sorrow. Lehi blesses him forever with a conditional inheritance, teaches lineage and promises, and assures that the fruit of Joseph's loins will not be utterly destroyed.

l: Moses, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Moses is raised up to deliver Israel from Egypt, receiving power in a rod, law written by the Lord, judgment, and a spokesman, while remaining unable to speak much.

l: the Messiah, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Messiah is awaited to come in the fulness of his own time. He will be made manifest to Israel’s branch, bringing light and freedom, and will come with power and glory to destroy enemies and recover believers; without Christ all men must perish.

l: the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The Lord is God, Christ, maker of the heavens and earth, Lord of Hosts, and the essential power for creation. He makes covenants and promises concerning Joseph’s seed, raises a choice seer and Moses, strengthens and preserves Joseph’s descendants, and gives commandments, prosperity for obedience, and cutting off for disobedience. He is merciful to seed, supports and teaches Nephi through visions, and gives liberally to those who ask rightly. He has power to redeem and deliver, displayed in his authority over sea, rivers, and heavens. He comforts Zion and his people, gives an enduring law, righteousness, and salvation, establishes and proves his words through witnesses, and teaches people his ways. He judges nations, the poor, the meek, and the wicked; rebukes many; humbles the proud; and is exalted alone. Because of iniquity, he forsakes the house of Jacob, yet later has mercy, recovers the remnant, gathers Israel and Judah, restores his people among all nations, and provides protection and refuge. His work culminates in judgment, the destruction of wickedness if necessary, and peace.

l: Joseph's brethren, The Second Book of Nephi
s: are_brought_to the restoration of Israel [through the work of the Lord] Joseph's brethren are the fruit of Joseph's loins, and the choice seer will do a work of great worth for them by bringing them to knowledge of the covenants.

l: house of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi
s: The house of Israel is a lineage and the Lord’s people, including Jews, the people of Nephi, and lost tribes led away. It is the subject of the Lord’s covenants and is portrayed as the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts. Its iniquities cause it to sell itself, and it is scattered, afflicted, hated, weary, and walking in darkness; the Lord seeks judgment from it but finds oppression. Yet its seed will not be utterly destroyed, and those broken off are remembered. In the latter days, the Messiah will be made manifest to it, it will be delivered and restored, come to know its Redeemer and the covenants, become a righteous branch, and be gathered home to lands of inheritance and possessions. Its written words will also be gathered together in one.

l: the fruit of Joseph's loins, The Second Book of Nephi
s: writes the writing The fruit of Joseph's loins will produce written words, receive the work of a choice seer, and be preserved because of the covenant. Its words will come together with the writings of Judah's descendants and will cry from the dust to later generations.

l: the fruit of Judah's loins, The Second Book of Nephi
s: writes the writing The fruit of Judah's loins will write, and its writing will grow together with the writing of Joseph's descendants to confound false doctrines, lay down contentions, and establish peace.

l: Judah, The Second Book of Nephi
s: Judah is a kingdom targeted by war from Syria, Ephraim, and Manasseh, yet its attackers’ plan fails and its adversaries are cut off. Its dispersed people are gathered, reconciliation with Ephraim ends envy and vexation, and Judah gains power over Edom and Moab.

l: a choice seer, The Second Book of Nephi
s: A choice seer from Joseph’s loins is raised up and highly esteemed among them. Commanded only by the Lord, he is like Moses, brings forth and confirms the Lord’s word to Joseph’s descendants, and helps bring salvation through the Lord’s power. Blessed and protected from destroyers, he is named after Joseph, Lehi’s last-born son, and his father.

l: the spokesman, The Second Book of Nephi
s: declares the writing [of the fruit of Joseph's loins] The spokesman will be made for the one raised up from Joseph's loins and will declare the writing produced by Joseph's descendants.

l: one mighty among them, The Second Book of Nephi
s: One mighty among Joseph's descendants, with exceeding faith, acts as an instrument in God's hands, works mighty wonders, does much good in word and deed, and brings restoration.

l: Egypt, The Second Book of Nephi
s: is_a_model_for Assyrian oppression [in the manner of Egypt] The remnant of the Lord’s people is recovered from Egypt. The Lord destroys the tongue of the Egyptian sea and makes men go over dry shod.
